body:
Fixes #408.

## What was wrong

On a dtplyr input, `summarize_with_margins(.margin_label = NULL)` returned a
factor dimension whose declared `NA` level had been dropped; the same call on
the same data through the local backend kept it. ADR 0012's sixth row promises
the level is preserved, and ADR 0016 places factor levels on the side
marginplyr constructs. Neither is qualified by backend.

## Root cause

`data.table`'s rbind drops a declared `NA` level from the result and turns the
values that used it into missing codes — for a list of one table as much as for
a union of branches:

```r
f <- structure(c(1L, 1L), levels = c("x", NA_character_), class = "factor")
a <- data.table::data.table(group = f)
levels(data.table::rbindlist(list(a))$group)
#> [1] "x"
```

The non-missing-label path never met that. A label is not one of the column's
levels, so its columns already crossed the union as character and were rebuilt
after it. A missing label adds no level, so its columns crossed as factors, and
the level was gone before restoration could keep it.

## The fix

A factor dimension whose Margin label is missing now takes the same
encode-and-rebuild route where the union would drop such a level. That is the
new `drops_na_factor_level_on_union` capability in `backend_capabilities()`,
granted to `dtplyr` alone.

The encoding has to be the sentinel one rather than `as.character()`: a value
on the `NA` level and the typed missing a margin row carries are both `NA` in
character, and the union is where the two would stop being distinguishable.
`margin_column_info()` decides it once per column as `encode_missing_label`, so
`label_margin_branch()` and `restore_margin_factors()` read one answer instead
of deciding twice.

## Backends other than dtplyr

Measured, and untouched. A plain duckdb round trip already drops the level
(`levels()` is `"x"` before any Margin verb runs), and `arrow` refuses the
column outright — `Invalid: Cannot insert dictionary values containing nulls`.
Both lose it before any branch exists, so ADR 0012's *local and
factor-preserving lazy adapters where supported* clause reaches dtplyr alone.

## Tests

The eight cases of ADR 0012's table had only ever run on a local data frame.
The table moved to a `factor_contract_cases()` helper and now runs on dtplyr
too, each case compared against the local result rather than against a literal.

A second test covers a value that *uses* the `NA` level, which no case in the
table does: it asserts the source row stays on the level (`is.na()` false) while
the margin rows are typed missing (`is.na()` true), for both
`summarize_with_margins()` and `expand_with_margins()`. That is what an encoding
which merely restored the levels would lose.

Row order is not asserted across backends: the two place a missing value within
one grouping set differently, which ADR 0018 leaves to the backend.

## Local checks

- `testthat::test_local()` with `NOT_CRAN=true`: 6373 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip.
- `lintr::lint_package()` after `pkgload::load_all()`: no lints.
- `.github/scripts/verify-context-budget.R`: within baseline.
- `roxygen2::roxygenise()`: no generated-file diff (no roxygen changed).

## [Codecov](https://app.codecov.io/gh/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/413?dropdown=coverage&src=pr&el=h1&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=github&utm_content=comment&utm_campaign=pr+comments&utm_term=Yusuke+Sasaki) Report
:white_check_mark: All modified and coverable lines are covered by tests.

:loudspeaker: Thoughts on this report? [Let us know!](https://github.com/codecov/feedback/issues/255)

## Review record

One round of `mattpocock-skills:code-review`, both axes, against
`git diff main...HEAD` at the merge-base `4f367b42bc506e491ad72e99edf0ecb3a3bc5c68`,
reading `dc5a921`. Answered in `1b83cf7`.

Standards sources passed: the sections of `AGENTS.md` the diff reaches (*Linting*,
*Documentation*, *Dependency metadata*, *Optional-dependency guards*, *Release matrix*,
*Queries against a lazy input*, *Code comments*), `CONTEXT.md`, ADRs 0012, 0015, 0016,
0018, 0020, and `design/architecture.md`'s *Answering a review* for what a finding about
prose may be.

### Standards — 3 findings, 2 smells

| Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `R/factor.R` — `missing_label_sentinels()`'s comment claimed the list is built once so both arms of a branch write the same string; the including arm called `factor_missing_sentinel()` again instead of reading it. False comment. | Fixed in code: `margin_factor_sentinels()` is keyed over every factor dimension and both arms read it. This also answers the *Duplicated Code* smell below — the derivation dropped from three sites to two, and the remaining one is `restore_margin_factors()`, on the other side of the union. |
| `R/backend-metadata.R` — "The backend is read here because this is the one place it is" is false: the same function reads `can_read_schema`, `can_restore_factors`, and `can_encode_factor_missing_values`, and `expand_margin_union()` reads `invents_row_on_column_add`. | Fixed in prose: the comment now says why the decision is settled there — neither side of the route is handed the backend. |
| Residual divergence, measured: a factor column with a declared NA level still loses it on dtplyr as a fixed `.by` key or as a passed-through column. | Ticket: #415. This branch's Acceptance is a Margin dimension, and #415 asks a question this branch does not — whether ADR 0016's promise boundary reaches a column marginplyr does not label. |
| *Duplicated Code* — the sentinel derived at three sites. | Fixed with the first finding. |
| *Duplicated Code* — the two eight-case loops assert the refusals differently (`conditionCall` vs `marginplyr_error`), so the two error rows were the one part of the contract not compared across backends. | Fixed in code: both loops now assert the call the refusal names. |

Checked and confirmed sound by the round, needing no change: `setNames`/`Filter` on empty
input; `margin_labels` keys always covering `factor_info`; `margin_factor_levels(info, NULL, …)`
passing `stopifnot` on `logical(0)`; dtplyr having no `native_grouping_sets`, so no path
reaches `restore_margin_factors()` without the branch encoding; no new execution entry
point (ADR 0020); the new test needing one backend (*Release matrix*).

### Spec — 1 finding

| Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|
| The nest verbs pass but nothing pinned them; the issue's *Not verified* asks whether the other Margin verbs reach the same branch-union path with the same result. | Fixed in code: the used-NA-level test covers all four Margin verbs. |

The round confirmed the issue's reproduction now prints its *Expected* section with
nothing else in the output changed, and independently measured the *Not verified*
backends — duckdb drops the level on the round trip before any branch, arrow errors on
ingest, sqlite returns character — so restricting `drops_na_factor_level_on_union` to
dtplyr is what ADR 0012's *factor-preserving lazy adapters* clause reaches. It found no
requirement implemented wrongly, having checked ordered factors with an NA level, a
named-list `.margin_label` mixing `NULL` with a label, `cube()` over two NA-level
dimensions, `.margin_label_position = "first"`, `.by` present, a `data.table` input,
`.check_margin_label = FALSE`, `.duplicates = "keep"`, and a level literally equal to the
sentinel string. It reported no scope creep.

### Local checks at `1b83cf7`

- `testthat::test_local()` with `NOT_CRAN=true`: 6373 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip.
- `lintr::lint_package()` after `pkgload::load_all()`: no lints.
- `roxygen2::roxygenise()`: no generated-file diff.

Correction to the record above: the full-suite count at `1b83cf7` is **6381** pass, 0 fail, 0 skip. 6373 was the count before the used-NA-level test was widened to all four Margin verbs in that same commit. The lint and roxygen lines are unchanged.

title: Keep a declared NA factor level across the dtplyr branch union
